title: The zero locus of an etale section is Zariski open
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $F$ be a sheaf of abelian groups on its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], with abelian sheaves as in [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], and let $p:V\to T$ be an etale object with $s\in F(V)$. There is a largest Zariski open subset $W\subseteq V$ on which $s$ restricts to zero. For every morphism $h:V'\to V$ in $T_{\Et}$, $s|_{V'}=0$ if and only if $h(V')\subseteq W$. For every geometric point $\bar v$ of $V$, the germ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] of $s$ in $F_{p\bar v}$ is zero if and only if the underlying point of $\bar v$ belongs to $W$.

source.place: Tag 04FR, lemma-zero-over-image, clauses (1)-(3); support complement as in Tag 04FT, lemma-support-section-closed (1)

proof.text: Every open subscheme $A\subseteq V$ is an object of $T_{\Et}$: its inclusion into V is etale and etale morphisms compose. Open coverings are jointly surjective etale coverings. Define $W=\bigcup\{A\subseteq V:A\text{ open and }s|_A=0\}$. This is a union indexed by a subset of the set of opens of V. On the open cover of W by these A, the two sections $s|_W$ and zero agree. The injectivity of the equalizer map in the sheaf axiom gives $s|_W=0$. Every zero open A is contained in W by construction, proving maximality. The empty cover gives $F(\varnothing)=0$, so the construction also handles an empty W.

source.place: Tag 04FR, proof of (1); union construction expands the cited Zariski sheaf argument

proof.text: Let $h:V\prime\to V$ be a morphism in $T_{\Et}$. Etale cancellation makes h etale. Its image $A=h(V\prime)$ is open by the open-map lemma. The factorization $V\prime\to A$ is a morphism between etale T-objects, hence etale by cancellation, and is surjective by the definition of A. Thus it is a singleton covering of A. If $s|_{V\prime}=0$, injectivity of $F(A)\to F(V\prime)$ from the sheaf equalizer gives $s|_A=0$, so $A\subseteq W$. Conversely, if $h(V\prime)\subseteq W$, h factors through the open subscheme W: the continuous map lands there and its structure-sheaf map restricts there. The restriction of s factors through $s|_W=0$, so $s|_{V\prime}=0$.

Fix a geometric point $\bar v$ of V and put $\bar t=p\bar v$. Compute the stalk using a small cofinal family of affine pointed neighbourhoods. Indeed the essentially-small-cover lemma provides a set of affine etale T-objects; for each such object its lifts of $\bar t$ form a set of morphisms. Their pairs form a small full subcategory J of all pointed neighbourhoods. Every pointed neighbourhood receives a pointed morphism from J: take an affine open $U$ containing its lifted point. Choose a representative $A$ and an isomorphism $e:A\to U$ over T. The lift to A is $e^{-1}\circ\bar u$, where $\bar u:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U$ is the factorization of the original lift; composing e with $U\hookrightarrow V$ gives the required pointed arrow (with V here denoting the chosen neighbourhood). The category of all pointed neighbourhoods is cofiltered; the full-subcategory lemma therefore makes J cofiltered and identifies the opposite-indexed colimit on J with the stalk colimit, compatibly with its coprojections. In particular choose a pointed affine refinement $(A,\bar a)\to(V,\bar v)$ from J, and let r be the restriction of s to A.

source.place: Tag 04FR, proof of (3); small affine indexing made explicit

proof.text: Assume the germ of s is zero. In the small filtered diagram $J^{\mathrm{op}}$, the coprojection sends r to this zero germ. Regard abelian groups and their homomorphisms as $\mathbf Z$-modules and linear maps, with $n\cdot x$ defined by repeated addition (and negatives); these descriptions have exactly the same objects, morphisms and colimit universal property. Apply the zero-detection clause of the filtered-module-colimit lemma with $R=\mathbf Z$. There is a pointed refinement $(B,\bar b)\to(A,\bar a)$ on which r restricts to zero. The composite $B\to V$ is a morphism of the small etale site, its restriction of s is zero, and it takes $\bar b$ to $\bar v$. Step 2 gives that its image lies in W. Hence the underlying point of $\bar v$ lies in W.

source.place: Tag 04FR, forward implication in (3); eventual zero criterion for the stalk colimit

proof.text: Conversely, if the underlying point of $\bar v$ belongs to W, the geometric point factors through W. The inclusion $(W,\bar v)\to(V,\bar v)$ is a pointed etale neighbourhood morphism. Since $s|_W=0$, the defining stalk coprojections identify the germ of s with the germ of zero, which is zero. Together with step 4 this proves the geometric-germ criterion for every geometric point, with no dependence on any chosen residue-field closure.
